title: Rural Walk-in Clinic Triage
seed_statement: We operate two rural walk-in clinics with rotating nurses and visiting physicians, and we need a consistent way to handle patient triage and urgent care handoffs during peak hours.

ground_truth.agency: Triage nurses perform initial severity classification. Visiting physicians review high-acuity cases before discharge. Clinic administrators handle scheduling and transport.
ground_truth.preconditions: All emergency Category 1 presentations must bypass triage and initiate immediate ambulance transfer. Patient consent for emergency care is presumed under standard medical necessity.
ground_truth.exceptions: When nurse and physician disagree on acuity, the higher acuity rating governs immediately. If visiting physician is delayed in transit, local nurse practitioner holds emergency stabilization authority.
ground_truth.cadence: Walk-in hours 8am to 6pm. Initial triage assessment must be completed within 10 minutes of patient arrival.
ground_truth.accountability: Every acuity override requires contemporaneous dual-signoff. Shift changeover requires a formal verbal and written patient handoff protocol.

scripted_responses: The triage nurses and rotating physicians are the main actors. Patients and their families are waiting in the front room.
Category 1 emergencies bypass our triage entirely and go straight to ambulance dispatch. That is our highest safety priority.
If a nurse and doctor disagree on urgency, our rule is the higher acuity classification always takes precedence immediately.
Triage cannot take more than ten minutes per patient or we violate our clinical accreditation standard.
When a physician is delayed on the highway, the lead nurse practitioner has stabilization authority until arrival.
At shift change, both incoming and outgoing clinicians must do an in-person bedside review for any patient pending transfer.
All overrides of a nurse's triage score must be countersigned by the attending physician before patient release.
